collection.description: The oldest known New Testament manuscript: a 2nd-century papyrus scrap of John 18 in the John Rylands Library, Manchester, both sides.

texts.title: P52 (John Rylands fragment): John 18:31-33, 37-38
texts.date_approx: c. 125-175 AD (NTVMR); mid to late 2nd century (Rylands catalogue)
texts.source: John Rylands Library, Manchester, Greek P 457 (P52): photographs from Manchester Digital Collections; Greek from the INTF NTVMR transcription; English from the King James Version
texts.description: The oldest known piece of a New Testament manuscript: a scrap of a papyrus codex of John, written in the 2nd century, with John 18:31-33 on one side and 18:37-38 on the other.

authors.name: Papyrus P52 (scribe)
authors.bio: Unknown scribe of a 2nd-century papyrus codex of the Gospel of John, of which one fragment (P52) survives in Manchester.
